_comment: A synthetic single-file static page. Written for this harness rather than copied from a real site: target-app source belongs to whoever owns it, and `sources/` is gitignored for that reason, so a fixture must not smuggle it back in. What it reproduces are the structural traits that make retrieval hard, each of which exercises a specific anchor kind: a bare <html> with no lang (TAG), content in a plain div with no landmark (CLASS from axe), a button whose rendered label differs from the design (TEXT), a title-case section name in unquoted prose (PHRASE), and a commented-out block that renders nowhere yet is the right answer. Every line number below was checked against the committed source/index.html.

violations.description: Ensure every HTML document has a lang attribute
violations.help: <html> element must have a lang attribute

violations.description: Ensure the document has a main landmark
violations.help: Document should have one main landmark

violations.description: Ensure all page content is contained by landmarks
violations.help: All page content should be contained by landmarks

finding.title: html-has-lang
finding.detail: The <html> element has no lang attribute, so screen readers cannot determine the document language.

expected.rationale: The bare <html> tag. A document-level rule with no id or class to anchor on - this is the case the TAG anchor kind exists for.

finding.title: landmark-one-main
finding.detail: The document has no main landmark, so keyboard users cannot skip to the primary content.

expected.rationale: The body and its top-level wrapper, where a <main> would be introduced. axe targets the whole document, so a location naming some div mid-page is wrong.

finding.title: region
finding.detail: Page content sits in a plain div rather than inside a landmark element.

expected.rationale: div.page-wrap, named directly in axe's target. Real DOM evidence behind a class anchor, so it should be the easiest of the three - and it is the case that caught stylesheets outranking markup on an alphabetical tie, since .page-wrap appears once in each file.

finding.title: Hero button label reads 'More info' instead of 'Enrol Today'
finding.detail: The primary call-to-action below the hero text is labelled 'More info →' in production, but the design shows 'Enrol Today'.

expected.rationale: button.cta-button.info and its label. Locatable only because 'More info' appears verbatim in the markup. The competing label is deliberately title-case: 'Enrol Today' extracts as both a quoted literal and a title-case phrase, and it also appears in the commented-out section 38 lines below. That is what makes this case catch two real bugs - line regions ignoring anchor weight, and one string counting twice when two rules both extract it - each of which landed this finding on the wrong block. A lowercase competing label does not reproduce either, which is why the wording here matters.

finding.title: Missing 'Enrol Today' section at the bottom of the page
finding.detail: The design shows an 'Enrol Today' section with a sign-up button below the gallery. Production ends at the gallery.
finding.likely_area: Bottom of page, below the gallery

expected.rationale: The commented-out enrol-section block. The hard case: the page renders none of this, so the only evidence is the quoted phrase appearing inside an HTML comment.

finding.title: Class Schedule entries do not match the design
finding.detail: The Class Schedule section lists different days and sessions than the design does.

expected.rationale: The heading and the cards under it. A title-case phrase lifted from unquoted prose - the PHRASE anchor kind.

finding.title: Footer social icons are missing
finding.detail: The design shows a row of social media icons in the footer. Production shows none.

expected.rationale: Deliberately unanswerable: this page has no social icons anywhere, in markup or comments. no_match is correct and a location here is a false positive. Without a case like this, a system that always guesses scores as well as one that knows when to stop.
